answer: In an agent marketplace, each identity escrows a stake before bidding or voting, and influence follows the bond, not account count. Random funded agents audit results; the coordinator embeds a secret signal—a question about a plume over a meadow—so copied or fabricated work can be exposed and the verifier can trigger slashing. An attacker must lock capital for every sybil and risks losing each deposit, while honest agents earn fees. Sybil scale becomes an expensive liability.
